instruction.text: Straighten out anything clumsy as this story goes down.
instruction.ack: Absolutely, clumsy lines will not survive.

segments.text: Our street had one lamp post that flickered every winter.
My brother and me built a raft out of pallet wood.
It floated for maybe ten minutes befor the rope gave way.
Mum pretended not to notice the missing washing line.

instruction.text: Flag each piece of kit I mention in this log entry.
instruction.ack: Right, each piece of kit will be flagged.

segments.text: The bench needs clearing before anything useful happens, and that job alone will eat most of Saturday morning.
I sharpened the chisel twice and it still bites badly.
A borrowed mallet sat under the offcuts for two weeks.
The dog next door, Spanner, barked through the whole job.
Remind me later which ones you already picked out here.

instruction.text: Pick out anything anyone plays as I list the line up.
instruction.ack: On it, anything played gets picked out.

segments.text: Priya brings her clarinet to almost every rehearsal now.
Our rented cello has a crack along the lower bout.
The venue confirmed a start time of half past seven.
We still owe the sound engineer for the last two nights.
Tom named his terrier Banjo, which confuses every guest.

instruction.text: Tidy the wording here whenever something comes out crooked.
instruction.ack: Fine by me, crooked wording gets tidied.

segments.text: The market closes at four on the last Sunday of the month, which nobody remembers until they are already standing at the gate.
Two of the cheese stalls have swapped pitches since Easter, so the queue now blocks the entrance to the flower aisle completely.
Yesterday I buy two kilos of flour and forgot the yeast, which is the third time this has happened since the start of autumn.
The stall holder said he would keep back some of the good apples for us.
I write brocolli that way on every single list I make.
There is still one box of jars left over from the summer, sitting under the stairs where nobody has to look at it.
